text: Which statement correctly distinguishes the metabolic roles of NAD+/NADH from NADP+/NADPH?
choices: NADP+/NADPH functions mainly in catabolism, while NAD+/NADH functions mainly in anabolism
NAD+/NADH functions mainly as an electron carrier in catabolism, while NADP+/NADPH functions mainly as an electron donor in anabolism
Both cofactors are used interchangeably in catabolic and anabolic pathways with no functional distinction
NAD+/NADH plays no role in glycolysis or the TCA cycle
explanation: NAD+/NADH is the electron carrier used in catabolic pathways such as glycolysis, the TCA cycle, and beta-oxidation, while NADP+/NADPH is the electron donor used in anabolic pathways such as fatty acid synthesis and the pentose phosphate pathway. This division keeps catabolic and anabolic redox pools separate; the reversed pairing, a claim of interchangeability, and the claim that NADH is absent from glycolysis/TCA are all incorrect.
